title: Saturation and distance correction
summary: When mutations pile up, raw distances mislead — corrections recover the tree.

prompts.concept: This example starts broken: at just 50 sites, JC69 already pushes several pairs past its p < 0.75 limit, so no tree can be built until you apply one of the fixes below.
prompts.math: JC69 needs p < 3/4. Once observed differences reach 0.75 the correction's logarithm has no finite answer.

prompts.concept: With a tree on screen, compare it with the true one. More sites sharpen the distance estimates; shorter branches or the p-distance are the other escapes from saturation.
prompts.math: p-distance always has a value, but it underestimates long branches because it ignores multiple hits.

prompts.concept: The corrected distance between two sequences diverges once their observed difference p nears 0.75 — under JC69 the estimate runs off to infinity, which is exactly what blocked the build at 50 sites.
prompts.math: d = −3/4·ln(1 − 4p/3): as p → 0.75 the logarithm's argument reaches 0, so the distance estimate has no finite value.
